answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one licensed low-power radio station broadcasting a daily signal sonnet — a fresh fourteen-line poem read aloud at a fixed hour and logged by independent listeners. Stations take their call signs from catalogued nebulae, one per person, with no bulk licences and an outside-money fee doubling per station on the same funding trail. Random spot-checks demand the holder read a new sonnet live on air within minutes, so one operator cannot staff two stations, and each extra fake costs another station, another live reader, and twice the prior fee.
